stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI used child porn to train Grok models, lawsuit says
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI is accused in a lawsuit of using child pornography to train its Grok models.
The training data allegedly included both real and AI-generated child pornography.
This represents a severe ethical and safety crisis regarding large language model training data.

stories.title: Report: Nvidia to acquire AI model repository Hugging Face for $13 billion
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Nvidia is reportedly acquiring Hugging Face, a key repository for open AI models.
The acquisition is valued at an estimated $13 billion.
This move signals Nvidia's strategic push to control critical infrastructure within the growing AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Anthropic's new hardware standard lets AI agents control the physical world
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Anthropic is introducing a new hardware standard for AI agents.
This standard aims to enable AI to directly control physical-world devices.
The core concept involves a standardized driver interface for device-to-AI communication.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current models being restricted to a single robot embodiment.
Allows models to leverage diverse, internet-scale video data from both human and robotic agents for generalizable physics learning.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes common ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 models achieve significant speed improvements (up to 90% faster) when run on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is enabled by Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) integrated within Ollama 0.31 and powered by MLX.
The speedup is particularly notable when utilizing the models with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, a popular tool for running local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: Anthropic was illegally blacklisted by the Trump administration, court rules
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: A court ruled that the Pentagon's blacklisting of AI company Anthropic by the Trump administration was unconstitutional.
The lawsuit alleged unlawful retaliation against Anthropic by the Trump administration.
The ruling marks a significant legal victory for Anthropic in its dispute with the former administration.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have made arrests related to the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP is identified as a prolific hacking group.
The group executed a large-scale supply-chain attack campaign affecting over 1,000 organizations.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk associated with LLM agents in product execution harnesses, where harmful tool use is a greater concern than simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current red-teaming methods, specifically the potential for retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack strategies.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES), an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining traceable, audited execution.
Achieves separation by placing persona in one trust domain and execution in another, linked by a governed contract bridge.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by simulating real-world corporate communication complexity without requiring sensitive data sharing.
The benchmark features an evaluation corpus exceeding 230,000 documents and tests LLMs across multiple dimensions of information retrieval.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA), a new token-level advertising mechanism.
Addresses the challenge of traditional advertising models in the age of generative AI.
Integrates advertiser influence directly into the language model's generation process via local continuation values.

stories.title: GLM-5.3 is now open-weight
stories.author: jeudesprits
bullet_points: GLM-5.3, a significant language model, has been released as open-weight.
The open-weight release is a major development in the AI/ML landscape.
This signals a potential shift towards more accessible and customizable large language models.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services and local, open-source LLMs.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia’s AI effects on everything
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: An unofficial version of Nvidia's DLSS 5 has reportedly leaked and is being utilized by modders.
The leaked code was found in an early-access build of NBA 2K27, allowing extraction of the AI upscaling technology.
Modders are actively integrating this experimental DLSS 5 technology into popular games like Cyberpunk 2077 and Skyrim.

stories.title: Meta addresses ‘pervert glasses’ reputation with a privacy fix and a new marketing campaign
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta is addressing privacy concerns related to its AI-powered smart glasses.
A software fix ensures the camera stops recording if the front-facing LED is covered.
The company is simultaneously launching a new marketing campaign to manage its public perception.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has updated its AI glasses software to address privacy concerns.
The update prevents the glasses from recording when the safety light is covered by the user.
This change is a response to increasing scrutiny over nonconsensual recording capabilities in consumer AI devices.

stories.title: AI industry says Trump plans to tax chips in the “single dumbest way imaginable”
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The AI industry is reacting negatively to proposed policies from Donald Trump.
The core of the concern is a plan to tax data centers as a strategy to compete in the AI race.
Industry experts view the proposed taxation method as highly detrimental or illogical.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences into reusable skills.
The system addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
It enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by systematically reusing learned skills.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using large-scale agent trajectory datasets for training LLMs on software issues.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve model performance by reducing the number of necessary trajectories while enhancing supervision quality.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM-based code review, which treats the process as a static, single-round task.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a dynamic, multi-round, and interactive manner, reflecting real-world development practices.
The research aims to improve the accuracy and realism of automated code review systems by modeling iterative developer-reviewer interactions.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions using discrete flow matching.
The approach models reactions not as molecular structure changes, but as transformations in electron occupation vectors.
This offers an alternative to current ML methods that rely on molecule generation or heuristic graph edits.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in current AI security scanner evaluations, which often only measure successful judgments.
It introduces a controlled benchmark using a synthetic corpus of 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts to test scanners like ModelScan and ModelAudit.
The research focuses on evaluating coverage and failure recovery, moving beyond simple pass/fail metrics in AI model security.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices.
A new method was developed to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The study is a retrospective analysis involving over 36,000 adult patients across two hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study uses six independent linear probes, one corresponding to each category of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT).
The goal is to determine if LLMs geometrically distinguish and relate different moral foundations (e.g., care/harm vs. fairness/cheat).

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices.
A novel machine learning model was developed to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The study utilized a large, retrospective dataset spanning two different hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between different moral foundations (based on Moral Foundations Theory - MFT).
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models, one for each MFT category (e.g., care/harm, fairness/cheat).

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for academia and open-source communities.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a model trained using a single RTX 5090, demonstrating a cost-efficient training approach.
Highlights the need for accessible, hardware-friendly, and open-source training recipes, contrasting with the multi-million dollar costs of existing models.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It addresses the lack of understanding regarding ES optimization behavior compared to established methods like GRPO.
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates a performance advantage of ES over GRPO in LLM reasoning tasks.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current scaling methods (like repeated generation) by leveraging structured patterns in LLM failure modes across model scales.
Aims to enhance reasoning performance while maintaining high computational efficiency.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows learned by AI agents.
It addresses the limitation where valuable insights guiding agent skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and reuse learned skills across multiple interaction iterations.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM training for software engineering: relying solely on successful agent trajectories can introduce noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance on real-world software issues by refining how training data is used.
The core innovation focuses on moving beyond simple trajectory collection to ensure the quality and efficiency of the steps used for supervised fine-tuning (SFT).

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of post-training methods (like RL/OPSD) in LLMs that require ground-truth labels.
It proposes Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO) as an alternative to traditional ground-truth reliance.
TTPO uses majority-vote pseudo-labels but addresses the inherent fragility and asymmetric failure modes of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a more realistic, multi-round, and interactive manner.
The research aims to capture the complex, iterative problem-solving nature of real-world software development reviews.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrowed reasoning coverage.
The proposed solution introduces a method using cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR.
This work offers an alternative to existing algorithmic regularizations for preserving LLM exploration during fine-tuning.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs distinguish between specific moral foundations (e.g., care/harm, fairness).
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models, one for each category derived from Moral Foundations Theory (MFT).

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in clinical NLP: models perform well in training but fail in real-world deployment due to overfitting to note artifacts.
Introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework designed to make clinical language models auditable.
Uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract sparse, human-interpretable features from Transformer activations to improve robustness.

stories.title: Stop Wrestling with ASR: The Complete Guide to Gemini 3.5 Transcribe 🎙️
stories.author: giom_v
bullet_points: The article focuses on a guide to using Gemini 3.5 for transcription tasks.
It addresses the challenges users might face when dealing with Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR).
It highlights Gemini's existing capabilities in analyzing long-form content like videos and podcasts.
